latest_evidence.probe: Immutable deterministic effect receipt created once with HTTP If-None-Match:* followed by mutable pointer advancement with strong If-Match CAS, compared against mutable-CAS-only state
latest_evidence.documented_contract: RFC 9110 section 13.1.2 states that If-None-Match:* makes an unsafe request such as PUT conditional on the target having no current representation, specifically to prevent competing initial creates; a false condition prevents the method and yields 412 for non-GET/HEAD methods. Section 13.1.1 requires strong comparison for If-Match and describes it as a lost-update defense for state-changing methods. Section 9.2.2 limits HTTP idempotency to the requested effect and permits other per-request side effects.
latest_evidence.tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification only. Assume a collision-resistant deterministic semantic effect key and an already-available origin/storage surface that correctly implements the stated HTTP preconditions. No origin server, hosted compute, paid/trial API, protected authority, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, or manual execution was used.
latest_evidence.mechanism_test: For an effect whose durable logical commit can be represented by an immutable receipt, derive the receipt URI from a canonical semantic effect key that excludes volatile fields such as timestamps. First attempt PUT receipt/<effect_key> with If-None-Match:*; concurrent or replayed attempts cannot create a second representation at the same key if the origin obeys RFC 9110. Then advance a mutable LATEST/pointer with strong If-Match. If the pointer CAS conflicts or the run ends after receipt creation, the immutable receipt survives and the pointer can be reconstructed on a later invocation, shrinking the lost-progress/replay window relative to mutable-CAS-only state. Using a content hash of a non-canonical body that includes volatile metadata is insufficient because same-intent replays can generate different names; semantic-key canonicalization is required.
latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: The two-layer pattern is a genuine transversal improvement for durable Chat-local/repository logical effects: create-once immutable receipts eliminate duplicate committed receipts for a stable semantic key, while a separate mutable CAS pointer becomes recoverable derived state rather than the sole proof of completion. It does not make an arbitrary out-of-band side effect exactly-once. A crash before receipt creation after an external effect leaves an unrecorded-effect window; a crash after receipt creation before the external effect leaves a recorded-but-unperformed window. RFC 9110 idempotency explicitly does not constrain unrelated side effects. Full arbitrary-side-effect atomicity therefore remains unresolved unless that effect itself accepts the same idempotency key or is transactionally coupled to the receipt.

candidate_comparison.tested_candidate: canonical semantic effect key -> immutable create-once receipt via If-None-Match:* -> mutable pointer via strong If-Match
candidate_comparison.baseline: mutable target-resource strong If-Match CAS only
candidate_comparison.expected_completion_time: low for internal repository/logical effects when an already-authorized conditional-create storage surface exists; unresolved if a new origin/service must be introduced
candidate_comparison.success_probability: high for duplicate committed-receipt suppression and crash-safe pointer reconstruction under the stated preconditions; insufficient for arbitrary external-effect exactly-once
candidate_comparison.conflict_duplication_risk: lower than mutable-CAS-only for same-intent replay because immutable receipt identity is stable and non-overwritable; pointer conflicts remain recoverable; external effect duplication remains unresolved
candidate_comparison.integration_cost: low to moderate for existing storage with conditional create/CAS; unacceptable for Phase-1 if it requires a new quota-bearing or paid origin
candidate_comparison.quota_fragility: No hosted quota was consumed in this probe. Full adoption remains conditional on using an already-authorized zero-cost, quota-independent transport rather than adding a service.

conflict_check: Exactly one bounded Phase-1 child; CLEAN role-local state plus official public RFC 9110 only; no O/downstream/other-worker/legacy/shared-ledger semantics; no scheduler mutation; no wait/poll/backoff/retry; no optional second leaf.
frontier: r257 established provider-neutral target-resource CAS with PUT plus strong If-Match and create-once semantics with If-None-Match:* but left arbitrary external-effect atomicity open.
r258 separates immutable semantic-effect receipts from a mutable pointer: the receipt is authoritative durable effect evidence, while the pointer is reconstructible derived state.
A stable semantic effect key must be canonical and exclude volatile receipt fields; raw content-addressing of timestamp-bearing bodies can fail to deduplicate same-intent replay.
The pattern reduces duplicate committed-receipt and pointer-loss windows for internal logical/repository effects without richer mode or finite quota.
Arbitrary external side effects still have before-receipt and after-receipt crash gaps unless the external system shares the same idempotency key or transaction boundary.
